item.title: Gambit 1.3.0
item.description:
# Gambit 1.3.0
Released November 21, 2026.
## Your Mac's agent, in your pocket
**The first browser where your phone drives the agent on your computer.**
Open a button beside Tabs on your iPhone and you are looking at your Mac. Not a mirror of a tab list — the actual page, live, and the actual agent, working on it.
- **The Mac's own pages, with the Mac's own sign-ins.** Ask for something and the turn runs *on the Mac*, on the tabs you are signed in to there. Nothing has to be re-authenticated on the phone, and nothing about your session leaves the Mac.
- **A live picture, not a screenshot.** A frame loop keeps the view current: a page in motion updates as fast as it can be encoded, a still one costs almost nothing. Pinch to zoom, double-tap to zoom where your finger is, or go full screen and read a PDF properly — a desktop page on a phone needs magnification, not a bigger box.
- **The transcript, as it happens.** Each step arrives as a sentence — "Read 4 results on Google Drive · 1.2s" — tap for the detail, and the agent's answers render as Markdown and tables, exactly as they do in the phone's own pane.
- **Read-only mirroring, by construction.** The phone can see your Mac; it cannot click, type or navigate on it. There is no route that accepts an action, so this is not a setting you can get wrong — it is the shape of the thing.
Ask the agent to switch tabs and the picture follows. That is the whole idea: the work happens where your browser already is, and the phone is the window onto it.
## Pairing that needs nothing installed
The phone now runs Gambit's own tailnet node, so a `.ts.net` pairing code works with nothing but Gambit on the device — no VPN profile, no second app, no account beyond the one you already signed in with.
It needed no VPN entitlement. The library Gambit links is a userspace network stack, not a packet tunnel, which was measured before a line of it was written.
- **Sign out of Tailscale**, from either app, when you want the Mac off your tailnet. Behind a confirmation, because a pairing made over the tailnet stops being dialable — the key is kept, the name is gone. - **Signing out no longer strands the node.** Sign-in pages are minted once in the lifetime of the process, so a node that had been signed out could never sign back in: the card spun for ever. It now asks again, and the page arrives in about a second.
## Share a tab, not your screen
When a page asks to share your screen — Meet, Zoom on the web, a Slack huddle — Gambit asks what to share, and offers **your tabs**. A tab is shared as its page alone, at 30 frames a second and 1920 pixels wide, and keeps coming while you go back to the call. No Screen Recording permission, and nothing of Gambit's own chrome in the picture.
## Web pages hear you, reliably
Calls in Gambit lost the microphone in several ways, all fixed: a second request while the bar was up was refused without asking, a call in a background tab was treated as hidden, and switching audio devices did not reach a call you were in. Now requests wait their turn, one Allow settles everything it covers, and when macOS refuses Gambit the microphone the bar says so with a button to fix it.
## Passkeys, passwords, and accounts
- **Passkeys** work beside 1Password and other WebAuthn extensions, and appear in the account list. - **The accounts popup** lists every saved account, searchable, without needing the Bitwarden extension. - **Passwords fill inside frames** — sign-ins embedded in a page, not just top-level ones. - **Suggest a strong password** on sign-up and change-password forms.
## The address bar
A Google search used to render in full: 227 characters, most of it protobuf base64, which looked exactly like a rendering fault — and was one. The pill now shows `google.com/search?q=your words`.
## Settings, shorter
Ten pages instead of fifteen, because a page that was a card or two now lives beside the page it belongs to: Downloads under General, Voice under Intelligence, Addons under Extensions, Updates under About. Advanced rows fold away, and settings that cannot apply are hidden rather than greyed out. Search finds everything where it now lives.
## Also fixed
- **Folders survive a second window.** Switching spaces in one window no longer takes the other window's Saved tabs out of their folders. - **Sign-in pages no longer refresh for ever.** A password manager's menu inside a sign-in field could reload a page every second, endlessly. - **Agents can name every tab by its id**, including the one-in-fifty whose id is all digits. - **A shared tab keeps 30 frames a second**, however long you share it. - **Cloud: another device can no longer undo your folders** — only what you changed by hand is sent, and a sync that would unfix more than ten kept tabs asks first. - **Gambit runs on Intel Macs**, and the website installs it on Windows and Linux too. - **Tabs switch without the window catching** on certificate prompts, spinners and saves. - **Trails and Tide are gone.** Today is always the plain list.
---
Everything, in detail, is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
